payload.problem_addressed: How to close the 'agentic coding loop' for robot manipulation programs without pre-supplied task specifications, primitives, or verification environments, inferring all three from a single visual human demonstration.
payload.method_summary: RAPID reconstructs a simulation environment and success predicates from one demonstration, represents manipulation primitives as object-centric relational trajectory-optimization programs (semantic roles + relations + effect parameter, resolved at runtime), composes primitives into a strategy via relational constraints, and iteratively executes-evaluates-diagnoses-revises both primitives and the composed strategy (plus synthesized scene variants) until a verifiable success predicate is satisfied for every case in the verification set.
payload.contributions_summary: RAPID automatically derives a testable task specification, action primitives, and an interactive verification environment from a single visual human demonstration, then uses a coding agent to construct, verify, and iteratively refine a reusable manipulation program. Its object-centric relational program representation expresses primitives as trajectory-optimization programs with runtime-resolved geometry, composed via relational constraints rather than fixed motions. On 8 nonprehensile manipulation tasks and the LIBERO-Pro benchmark, RAPID substantially outperforms code-as-policies and agentic baselines and transfers effectively to a real Franka arm.
key_architecture_choices: Object-centric relational program representation: primitives P_i=(G_i,C_i,Ψ_i,ρ_i,J_i) with semantic roles, relations, effect parameter, success predicate, geometry resolver, and optimization cost
Strategies compose primitives via relational connecting constraints c_k evaluated just-in-time from the prior phase's outcome, keeping frozen primitives reusable across scenes
Shared VerifyRevise loop: ExecuteEvaluate then DiagnoseRevise repeated until AllSuccessful on demo + synthesized feasible scene variants
Cross-entropy method (gradient-free) trajectory optimizer within each primitive
VLM + SAM3 + SAM3D + FoundationPose pipeline to reconstruct an interactive simulation environment from a single RGB-D demonstration frame
datasets: 8 custom contact-rich nonprehensile manipulation tasks (simulation + real Franka Research 3)
LIBERO-Pro (extension of LIBERO with position and instruction perturbations)
metrics: Success rate (mean ± std over 3 trials, MuJoCo simulation)
Real-robot success rate over 10 test scenes per task
payload.headline_results: RAPID reaches 0.759 average success on the 8 nonprehensile tasks vs 0.013-0.146 for CaP/CaP-Agent0 baselines; achieves highest success on 5 of 6 LIBERO-Pro settings; deploys effectively on a real Franka arm where CaP-Agent0 struggles.
claimed_advantages: Generalizes across object appearance, pose, geometry, physical properties, and scene configuration from a single demonstration
Requires no pre-specified success signals, human-engineered primitives, or resettable environments
Construction cost is amortized: one-time cost of tens of minutes per task, then semantic binding at deployment takes only seconds
limitations: Construction takes on the order of tens of minutes per task (one-time synthesis cost)

On LIBERO-Goal (Pos.), RAPID ranks second behind ASPIRE, which is given a specialized interpolate-segment primitive for articulated-object manipulation RAPID must discover from only a single debug scene
Relies on VLM/SAM3D scene reconstruction and FoundationPose registration quality for the real-to-sim step
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The shared VerifyRevise loop (execute candidate program against a verification set, diagnose failure, revise, repeat until AllSuccessful) is a directly transferable pattern for hexgen: gate revision of a rejected best-of-N candidate on the frozen verifier's structural-validity signals (compiles, zero inverted elements, quality/fidelity bounds) instead of manipulation success predicates. The relational-interface mechanism, where a primitive declares typed semantic roles r_i and relations Γ_i and a runtime binding b∈Bind_E(r_i,Γ_i) assigns scene entities satisfying those relations, is a close conceptual analog to pointer/copy-head addressing that is constrained to satisfy face-adjacency relations in the B-rep graph — worth borrowing as a template for relation-constrained pointer decoding.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is robot manipulation, not CAD/mesh generation, so applicability is at the level of the agentic verify-revise architecture and relational program representation, not any mesh-specific mechanism. RAPID uses an off-the-shelf coding LLM agent (Codex/GPT-5.6) as the program author via in-context revision rather than a trained autoregressive network, so it is not directly reusable code/weights, only a design pattern.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: M — the verify/revise loop and relational role-binding idea are conceptually portable but would need reimplementation for a compiled hex-meshing DSL and a trained (not LLM-agent) decoder.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol) as the coding agent
SAM 3 / SAM 3D for segmentation and mesh reconstruction

payload.problem_addressed: Whether off-the-shelf coding agents can automate generalized task-and-motion-planning (TAMP) engineering by synthesizing, from a task description and simulator interaction alone, a single frozen program per environment that solves unseen problem instances without further TAMP-specific scaffolding.
payload.method_summary: Each coding agent (Claude Code/Opus 5, Codex/GPT-5.6 Sol, Codex/GPT-6 Astra) is given a task description and client access to reset/step simulator functions inside a sandboxed container, with a fixed $20 synthesis budget; it freely chooses experiments to run, writes/executes code, and revises a programmatic policy (reset + get_action class) using only interaction feedback, no hand-designed predicates/operators/samplers. The resulting program is frozen and evaluated LLM-free on 100 held-out instances per environment across 28 KinDER/PDDLStream environments; a '+source' variant additionally exposes environment source code.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper presents a large-scale, systematic study (AgenticGenPlan) showing that off-the-shelf coding agents, given only a task description and simulator interaction (no hand-engineered TAMP predicates, operators, samplers, or skills), synthesize generalized programmatic policies that outperform hand-engineered TAMP planners, one-shot LLM generation, and an LLM-based generalized-planning baseline across 28 simulated environments spanning kinematic/dynamic 2D/3D tasks. Agents use targeted interaction to calibrate physical models, probe edge cases, and iteratively refine strategies, sometimes discovering unexpected manipulation strategies not seen in prior published solutions.
key_architecture_choices: Programmatic policy interface: a frozen class exposing reset() and get_action(h_t) implementing π(h_t), with no imposed abstraction (search, sampling, symbolic planning left to the agent)
Sandboxed Docker container with client-only simulator access (reset/step), no network, bare Python+NumPy/SciPy in the main setting to force self-contained program synthesis
Fixed $20 model-usage synthesis budget per run, 5 independent runs per method per environment
Agent commits the evolving program to git before each test, enabling replay of the revision trajectory
'+source' ablation setting exposing environment source code to isolate the benefit of agentic interaction vs. information access
datasets: KinDER benchmark (25 environments: Kinematic2D, Dynamic2D, Kinematic3D, Dynamic3D)
metrics: Success rate on 100 held-out instances per environment (mean and [min-max] over 5 runs)
Comparison against hand-engineered TAMP planner, one-shot LLM generation, and LLMGenPlan baseline
payload.headline_results: All three agent configurations beat hand-engineered planners on the 16 environments with one available: Claude Code (Opus 5) averages 82% success (1.7x the planner's 47%), Codex/GPT-6 Astra averages 95%, Codex/GPT-5.6 Sol averages 56%; agents also use an order of magnitude less computation per instance than the planners as object counts grow.
claimed_advantages: Coding agents require far less TAMP-specific engineering than existing generalized-TAMP methods (no hand-designed predicates/operators/samplers/skills)
Programs discover unexpected, non-prehensile strategies absent from prior published solutions on these benchmarks, evidence against simple memorization
Programs are much faster at test time than TAMP planners (2.1s/0.5s per instance for Opus/Astra vs 29s for planners) despite requiring no per-instance replanning
limitations: Some dynamic 3D environments requiring sweeping or pouring many small objects remain largely unsolved in the main (no-source) setting
Setup assumes fully observed, object-centric states and simulator access during synthesis; does not establish performance under perception uncertainty
Models' training data are undisclosed, so prior exposure to benchmark code cannot be fully excluded (though synthesis logs show substantial iterative revision, arguing against pure recall)
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core experimental design — give an agent interaction/simulator access and a frozen synthesis budget, let it freely choose what to probe and test, then freeze the program and evaluate on held-out instances with no further LLM calls — is a close methodological analog to using an LLM-agent authoring pipeline as a training-data source for hexgen: an agent could similarly interact with the deterministic mesher/verifier to synthesize or repair hex-meshing DSL programs for held-out B-rep instances, distilling the resulting verified programs into imitation-learning targets for the 27M-parameter decoder. Their finding that agents calibrate internal physical/geometric models purely through interaction (e.g., fitting 6 kinematic parameters from probing) is a useful precedent for execution-guided repair of a model's own broken rollouts.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is a study of general-purpose LLM coding agents as the synthesis mechanism, not a trained neural decoder; transfer to hexgen is at the level of the evaluation protocol and agentic-authoring-as-data-source idea, not any specific architecture or DSL mechanism. Programs are per-environment (not conditioned on a graph-structured input like a B-rep), so there's no direct pointer/copy-head or graph-transformer analog here.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: M — straightforward to adapt the harness (freeze-and-evaluate protocol, git-commit revision trace) for generating/distilling hexgen training programs via an LLM-agent-in-the-loop, but building the sandboxed verifier-interaction environment is nontrivial engineering.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra
KinDER benchmark and baseline planner implementations
LLMGenPlan (re-implemented) as a non-agentic LLM generalized-planning baseline

provenance.problem_addressed: We investigate whether coding agents can automate this process by synthesizing programs that generalize across instances.
provenance.method_summary: The program is then frozen and evaluated on unseen instances, with no LLM involved at test time.
provenance.contributions_summary: coding agents are surprisingly effective at generalized TAMP: all three agent configurations outperform hand-engineered planners
provenance.headline_results: Claude Code averages 82% success, 1.7 times the planner's 47%, and Codex averages 95% with GPT-6 Astra and 56% with GPT-5.6 Sol.
provenance.claimed_advantages: strategies absent from any published solution are hard to attribute to memorized training data
provenance.limitations: some dynamic three-dimensional environments are still largely unsolved in the main setting, particularly those that require sweeping or pouring many small objects

payload.problem_addressed: Whether a model can learn to generate its own most-useful training data from zero natural data, by casting synthetic data generation as a search over the space of all computable structure (inspired by Solomonoff induction), providing an effectively unbounded, compute-limited (rather than human-knowledge-limited) source of pretraining signal.
payload.method_summary: Two randomly-initialized transformers co-evolve: a generator proposes byte-emitting programs for a minimal universal (Brainf*ck-like) Turing machine; a learner is trained by standard next-token cross-entropy on the executed programs' byte outputs. The generator is trained by policy-gradient RL (GRPO-style, KL-regularized toward a Solomonoff-like uniform program prior) using a 'learning-progress' reward: the alignment between a program's induced learner gradient and the learner's own recent (AdamW-preconditioned) parameter-movement trajectory, which concentrates the generator on programs at the frontier of what the learner can currently learn. A program pool mixes fresh generator samples, local mutations, and replayed high-reward programs, and expert-iteration (reward-weighted SFT) distills good programs back into the generator to prevent forgetting.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data, in which a generator and learner bootstrap entirely from random initialization with no natural data, using a universal Turing machine as the program space and a learning-progress RL reward to keep the generator's outputs at the frontier of the learner's capability. Across held-out natural datasets spanning text, images, audio, speech, music, and DNA, the resulting learner exhibits predictable zero-shot power-law loss scaling in self-play compute, with exponents comparable to direct training on natural data, plus emergent in-context learning and discovery of recognizable mathematical program families (arithmetic, Fibonacci, geometric, quadratic, cubic sequences) during training.
key_architecture_choices: Generator and learner are identically-architected decoder-only Llama transformers, both trained from random initialization (tabula rasa)
Program substrate is a minimal Turing-complete Brainf*ck-like language over a byte-valued tape; byte-level tokenization (256-value vocabulary) for modality-agnostic evaluation

Generator reward is a preconditioned gradient-alignment score between a program's induced learner gradient and the learner's AdamW-preconditioned parameter movement over a growing lookback window, avoiding the degenerate 'just make it hard to predict' reward

GRPO-style batch-level policy-gradient objective with KL regularization toward a fixed Solomonoff-style uniform program prior, plus sequence-level importance-ratio correction for off-policy replay/mutation samples

Program pool mixes fresh samples, local mutations of high-reward programs, and replayed earlier programs; expert-iteration (reward-weighted SFT) distills the pool back into the generator to mitigate catastrophic forgetting
datasets: Held-out natural evaluation sets: text (DCLM), images, RAW audio/speech, music, DNA, formal mathematics (Metamath), C source code
metrics: Zero-shot validation loss (bits per byte) fit to a compute-optimal power law L(C)=E+AC^-α
Epiplexity (extractable structure per compute-bounded learner) of generator-produced corpora
In-context-learning success rate under greedy decoding vs. number of ICL examples on reverse-string, stack, associative-recall, and arithmetic (max/min/sum) tasks
payload.headline_results: Self-play produces predictable power-law zero-shot loss scaling in compute across text, images, music, audio, speech, and DNA with exponents comparable to direct natural-data pretraining; a fixed universal-prior baseline over the same program space scales far more slowly; self-play models show near-100% ICL accuracy on reverse-string/stack/associative-recall tasks where PCFG- and universal-prior-pretrained models largely fail.
claimed_advantages: Provides an effectively unbounded, compute-rather-than-human-knowledge-limited source of pretraining signal
The adaptive (self-play) curriculum scales substantially faster than sampling from the same universal program space with a fixed, non-adaptive prior

Learns generic transferable predictive structure (e.g. copying, recursion, hierarchical composition) rather than a single domain's inductive bias, giving broader cross-modality transfer than a hand-designed synthetic prior (e.g. PCFGs, strong on language but weak on images/audio/music)
limitations: Experiments are confined to models below 25M parameters at 4K context; unclear whether the results persist at larger scale
Universal pretraining cannot recover contingent (world-specific) information — facts must still enter through interaction with the world / natural data
PCFG pretraining remains stronger than self-play specifically on text and code, domains its hand-designed inductive bias matches well
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core mechanism — a generator trained by RL with a learning-progress reward to produce synthetic (input, target) pairs at the frontier of what the learner can currently master, replacing a fixed/random data-generating prior with an adaptive curriculum — is directly transferable to hexgen's 'inverse factory': instead of sampling uniformly random valid programs, an RL-trained generator could be shaped to propose B-rep/program pairs whose difficulty tracks the decoder's current capability, potentially improving data efficiency and coverage versus the current random-sampling data synthesis strategy. The self-play program pool's mix of fresh samples, mutations of high-reward programs, and experience replay is also a reusable recipe for curriculum-managing synthetic (B-rep, program) generation.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is a pretraining-methodology paper (predicting raw bytes from a universal Turing machine), not about B-rep encoders, pointer/copy mechanisms, or mesh validity; the transferable idea is specifically the adaptive, gradient-alignment-based learning-progress curriculum for synthetic data generation, not the architecture or byte-level tokenization itself. The learning-progress reward computation (Eq. 2) requires access to per-program learner gradients, which may be a nontrivial engineering cost to replicate for a 27M-parameter program-generation setting.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: L — adapting the RL-trained, gradient-alignment-reward generator-learner co-training loop to hexgen's inverse-factory data synthesis would be a substantial new training system, not a drop-in component.
dependencies_on_other_methods: GRPO-style policy-gradient RL objective (Guo et al., 2025)
AdamW optimizer state used as the preconditioner in the reward
Forward-mode automatic differentiation to compute gradient-alignment reward without materializing full gradients

provenance.problem_addressed: A more general approach to pretraining would let the model learn to generate the data most useful for its own improvement.
provenance.method_summary: The generator is trained via reinforcement learning to propose programs near the frontier of the learner's capabilities, measured by how strongly the learner's gradients align with the learner's recent learning trajectory
provenance.contributions_summary: Across several natural datasets, zero-shot loss exhibits predictable scaling in compute. The models also exhibit in-context learning, and discover recognizable mathematical sequences during training.
provenance.headline_results: self-play exhibits predictable scaling across images, melody, audio, speech, text, and code despite using minimal inductive bias
provenance.claimed_advantages: fixed sampling scales substantially more slowly, demonstrating that access to a universal program space alone is not enough
provenance.limitations: The experiments reported here are confined to models below 25M parameters at a 4K context

payload.problem_addressed: Classical hierarchical (X-armed) bandit search over a tree requires a smoothness schedule specified in advance, but real objectives (e.g. LLM routing, prefix caching, test-time search, prompt trimming) are typically only piecewise smooth with sharp discontinuities near the optimum, so a global smoothness assumption either prunes promising regions or forfeits hierarchical savings.
payload.method_summary: CANOPY frames each tree-structured decision problem (model routing, prefix caching, test-time search, top-k identification, prompt trimming) as a multi-fidelity bandit over a complete tree with cheap biased internal-node 'probes' (random-path samples giving the subtree average) and expensive unbiased leaf evaluations. It computes an online, data-driven certificate (via a log-sum-exp/MGF bound combined with empirical-Bernstein confidence intervals) of each node's aggregation bias, flags cells where the measured within-cell spread exceeds the assumed Lipschitz floor as containing a discontinuity, and directs expensive leaf-level evaluation only to flagged cells while running the standard optimistic tree descent with the certified bias bound elsewhere.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces CANOPY, a multi-fidelity tree bandit that certifies local smoothness directly from cheap random-path probes rather than assuming or searching over a global smoothness schedule, and directs expensive leaf evaluations toward cells where the certificate detects a violation. It proves fixed-budget identification and regret guarantees whose extra cost over the smooth-tree rate is additive in the number of discontinuities, and shows empirically across twelve benchmarks (routing, top-k identification, test-time search, caching, prompt trimming) that this consistently improves matched-budget performance, including 2.9x higher top-10 recall on a 1000-model pool and 1.6x more SWE-bench Verified issues resolved than best-of-N.
key_architecture_choices: Multi-fidelity tree model: internal-node 'probe' returns a random-path sample with expectation equal to the cheap subtree average; leaf 'evaluation' is the expensive unbiased signal

Online local-Lipschitz aggregation-bias certificate combining a log-sum-exp/moment-generating-function bound on the max-minus-mean gap with empirical-Bernstein confidence bounds (Maurer & Pontil), proof mechanized in Lean 4

Discontinuity-guided adaptive sampling: cells whose certified within-cell spread exceeds the Lipschitz floor Lρ^ℓ are flagged and receive full fixed-budget best-arm identification treatment instead of the smooth aggregation bound

Applies the same optimistic tree-descent index (upper confidence bound + certified/flagged bias bonus) used by classical HOO/X-armed bandits, but with the bias term replaced by the data-driven certificate
datasets: RouterBench, LLMRouterBench, RouterEval (1000-model pool) for routing/identification
MMLU (live routing), τ-bench retail (long-horizon tool agents)
MATH, GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, MBPP, SWE-bench Verified for test-time search
Mooncake production caching traces; a live vLLM server
metrics: Task accuracy / official resolved-issue rate at matched generation calls (search)
Tokens/blocks reused per request and time-to-first-token at matched cache memory (caching)
payload.headline_results: 2.9x higher top-10 recall vs. the best structure-blind baseline on a 1000-model pool; 1.6x more SWE-bench Verified issues resolved than best-of-N (up to 1.8-2.2x in tight-budget cells); +0.087/+0.111 accuracy gains on MATH/GPQA-Diamond; 3.6x lower median time-to-first-token with adaptive prefix caching; adaptive cache reuses 78% more blocks than LRU after a popularity shift.
claimed_advantages: Certifies the required smoothness information directly from cheap data rather than assuming or searching over a schedule (prior work showed this is impossible from leaf evaluations alone)

Extra cost over the smooth-tree rate is provably additive in the number of discontinuities K, recovering the clean Lipschitz rate at K=0 and degrading gracefully to structure-blind search as violations become dense
Unifies five apparently distinct LLM-inference problems (routing, caching, trimming, identification, search) as instances of the same budgeted multi-fidelity tree-optimization problem
limitations: Advantage vanishes when regions are homogeneous (e.g. ties the flat learner on RouterEval; a single cheap model dominates on LLMRouterBench)
No gain when the task is saturated (near-zero gap on GSM8K) or when the achievable optimum is out of reach for a weak model (loses to best-of-N on MATH with Llama-3.1-8B)
No benefit when the workload is stationary/prefixes barely overlap (caching) or when a benchmark leaves no headroom to trim (e.g. MMLU trimming only beats the verbose default)
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: CANOPY's core mechanism — treat autoregressive generation as a tree where every prefix is a node, use cheap biased internal-node signals to certify where a smoothness/value assumption locally holds, and concentrate expensive exact evaluation (here, the frozen structural-validity verifier) only on flagged, uncertain prefixes — is a directly transferable template for MCTS/beam-style value-guided search over hexgen's program prefixes: rather than a fixed rollout/verification budget per node, a data-driven certificate could decide where cheap heuristic scores (e.g. partial-program feasibility estimates) are trustworthy versus where a full verifier run (compile + mesh + quality check) is needed, reducing best-of-N verifier calls at matched compute.
payload.reviewer_notes: Applied entirely to LLM-serving and search settings (routing, caching, trimming, math/code search), not to program or geometry generation, so the bridge is purely at the level of the tree-search/certification algorithm, not any domain-specific mechanism. The guarantees assume leaf-mean sub-Gaussianity and a dispersion condition on discontinuities (Balcan et al., 2018) that would need to be checked or approximated for the very different reward landscape of mesh-program validity.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: M — the certificate and discontinuity-guided sampling algorithm are self-contained and could be adapted as a search-time wrapper around the existing best-of-N + frozen-verifier screening without touching the decoder itself.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Classical optimistic tree-bandit / X-armed bandit algorithm (HOO, Bubeck et al. 2011)
Dispersion condition for piecewise-smooth optimization (Balcan et al., 2018)
Fixed-budget best-arm identification theory (Kaufmann et al., 2016; Audibert et al., 2010)

provenance.problem_addressed: Hierarchical bandit methods can exploit this structure, but typically require a specific smoothness schedule to be specified in advance, even though real objectives are often only piecewise smooth
provenance.method_summary: CANOPY uses cheap random-path probes to construct an online certificate of local aggregation bias, then directs expensive leaf evaluations toward cells where the certificate detects a smoothness violation.
provenance.contributions_summary: We prove fixed-budget and regret guarantees whose additional cost is additive in the number of discontinuities
provenance.headline_results: 2.9× higher top-10 recall on a 1000-model pool, 1.6× more SWE-bench Verified issues resolved than best-of-N
provenance.claimed_advantages: to our knowledge, are the first to certify the required smoothness information directly from data rather than assume it or search over candidate schedules
provenance.limitations: When regions are homogeneous there is no structure to exploit. RouterEval ties the flat learner

payload.impact_rationale: The verify-revise-until-passing loop and relation-constrained runtime binding are a useful architectural template but not a drop-in technique with quantified gains for structural validity or mesh quality.
payload.effort_rationale: Conceptually portable but needs full reimplementation for a compiled hex-meshing DSL and a trained (non-LLM-agent) decoder rather than an in-context coding agent.

payload.impact_rationale: Strong precedent that an LLM-agent, given interaction access to a verifier/simulator and a freeze-and-evaluate protocol, can synthesize generalizable programs — directly motivates using agent-authored/repaired programs as a hexgen training-data source, but it is an evaluation study, not a specific transferable algorithm.
payload.effort_rationale: Would require building an analogous sandboxed interaction harness (agent probes the mesher/verifier, freezes a program, evaluates on held-out B-reps) as a data-generation pipeline — a real engineering project.

payload.impact_rationale: An RL-trained generator that keeps synthetic data at the learner's capability frontier could materially improve the inverse factory's data efficiency/coverage over uniform random program sampling if it worked as well for structured B-rep/program pairs as for byte sequences.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires building a new generator-learner co-training loop with a gradient-alignment RL reward and program pool/replay machinery — a substantial standalone training system, not a wrapper.

payload.impact_rationale: A data-driven certificate for deciding where cheap heuristics are trustworthy vs. where a full verifier run is needed could reduce verifier/mesher calls per generation at matched compute during best-of-N or beam/MCTS decoding over program prefixes.
payload.effort_rationale: The certificate and discontinuity-guided sampling algorithm are self-contained and could be added as a search-time wrapper around existing best-of-N screening without touching the decoder itself.
